Subject: Calendar invite shows shifted hour after scheduling

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the quick demo link — I used the Calendly page you sent and picked Wednesday at 10:00, Paris time. I just accepted the Google invite but it landed in my calendar as 02:00 (AM) on the same day.

Screenshot attached (I exported the ICS and saw the DTSTART as 20270331T020000Z). Does Redwood's scheduling page default to UTC somewhere? I want to make sure our whole team in Paris (CET) joins at 10:00 local.

A couple quick asks: can you confirm the slot is 10:00 CET? If Calendly is sending a UTC-based invite we might miss it. If needed we can do a manual invite from our side, but would prefer to keep it standard.

Thanks — Lucie

Subject: Re: Calendar invite shows shifted hour after scheduling

Hi Lucie — really appreciate the heads-up and sorry for the confusion. Short answer: the Calendly flow should respect the visitor locale, but a timing edge can happen when our event template was created in UTC and a DST boundary / locale mismatch occurs.

I'm looping in Hannah from Sales Ops to confirm the booking and send a manual invite while we fix the scheduling template. Practical options now:

- Quick fix (recommended): Hannah will send a manual .ics from our calendar set to 10:00 CET and attach the file. If you accept that invite it should display correctly for everyone in Paris.
- Workaround (if you prefer Calendly): On the scheduling page there is a timezone dropdown at the top-right — please confirm it shows "Europe/Paris" before you confirm. If it shows UTC, switch it to your local timezone and then rebook.
- Fallback: We can create a Chili Piper fallback route that generates a local-time invite (we've used it for APAC customers before).

I've attached a one-page agenda for the demo so you can share with your attendees. Hannah — can you generate the manual .ics for 2027-03-31 10:00 Europe/Paris and send to Lucie? Also please update the Calendly event settings to prefer visitor locale / show timezone prominently.

Thanks,
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Lucie Moreau <lucie.moreau@acme-analytics.eu>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Calendar invite shows shifted hour after scheduling

Hi Lucie & Vivek,

Thanks for flagging — I dug into the Calendly event. The event's timezone was set to UTC at creation (legacy template). I changed the event owner settings to prefer the invitee's timezone display and updated the event timezone to Europe/Paris.

I also created a manual invite and attached the .ics (acme-demo-invite.ics). The invite is for:
- Date: 31 Mar 2027
- Time: 10:00 — 11:00 Europe/Paris (CET, UTC+1)
- Conference: Zoom link will be added when you accept the invite

Notes on behavior we saw: when a template's base timezone is UTC, some calendar clients will write DTSTART in Zulu (UTC) and the conversion can show an unexpected hour for participants in GMT+1 if DST flags don't match the event's timezone metadata. Changing the event's timezone + sending a manual ICS avoids that.

Attachment: acme-demo-invite.ics (manual invite)

Lucie — if you accept that invite it should appear as 10:00 for everyone in Paris. If any of your team are joining from London or remote US we can add explicit timezone notes in the body.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

Perfect — thanks both. I accepted the manual invite and it shows as 10:00 — all good on our side. I also verified the Calendly link now shows Europe/Paris in the dropdown.

Two quick follow-ups:
- Please include the Zoom link in the final invite body (our security team requires an explicit link in the calendar event).
- For future bookings, could you add a short note on the Calendly page: "If you see a different time, please check the timezone selector in the top-right" — that would save confusion for international guests.

Looking forward to the demo on Wednesday.

Best,
Lucie
